description: Reusable editorial style packs that overlay base rules
corpus_note: Numeric dialogue_ratio values calibrated to corpus statistics from age-appropriate texts

minimalist.label: Minimalist
minimalist.description: Clean, direct prose with short sentences. Inspired by Hemingway's iceberg theory.
guidance: Use short, direct sentences
Minimize adjectives and adverbs
Avoid figurative language and similes
Focus on concrete actions over descriptions
Let actions speak for themselves
Show emotions through behavior, not explanation
Keep paragraphs tight—2-3 sentences maximum
Use strong, specific verbs instead of adverb+verb

cinematic.label: Cinematic
cinematic.description: Visually rich prose with sensory detail. Writes like a camera capturing a scene.
guidance: Open scenes with establishing details like a camera shot
Include visual details: colors, light, shadows, movement
Add sounds: dialogue, ambient noise, character sounds
Include texture and physical sensations when characters interact
Use action verbs that create mental images
Simple similes allowed (like, as)
Vary sentence length for rhythm: short for tension, longer for atmosphere
Show the environment changing as characters move through it

humorous.label: Humorous
humorous.description: Light, playful tone with age-appropriate humor. Makes readers laugh out loud.
guidance: Use concrete, situational humor based on relatable scenarios
Set up expectations, then subvert them
Include funny dialogue with distinct character voices
Use exaggeration for comic effect
Build toward comic moments with proper setup
Use repetition with variation for running gags
End scenes on laugh lines when possible
Keep descriptions brief—focus on the funny parts

humor_techniques.timing: Short sentences for punchlines. Pause before the funny part.
humor_techniques.contrast: Serious setup + silly payoff, or vice versa
humor_techniques.specificity: Specific details are funnier than vague ones
humor_techniques.character_reaction: Show characters' funny reactions to situations

sel_focused.label: SEL-Focused
sel_focused.description: Social-emotional learning emphasis with explicit emotion labeling. Teaches emotional intelligence through story.
guidance: Name emotions explicitly using feeling words
Show characters noticing physical signs of emotions (tight chest, warm face)
Include moments where characters pause to recognize their feelings
Model healthy coping strategies (deep breaths, counting, talking)
Show characters considering how others might feel
Include dialogue where characters express feelings appropriately
Demonstrate that all feelings are okay, but not all actions are
Show emotional growth from beginning to end of story

self_awareness.description: Characters identify and name their emotions
examples: Maya noticed her heart was beating fast. She felt nervous.

self_management.description: Characters use strategies to manage strong feelings
examples: She counted to ten before speaking.
I wonder how that made her feel.
He tried to see things from her point of view.

relationship_skills.description: Characters communicate effectively and resolve conflicts
examples: I feel hurt when you say that.
Can we talk about what happened?
What might happen if I do this?
She thought about how her choice would affect others.

adventure.label: Adventure
adventure.description: Fast-paced, action-oriented storytelling. Keeps readers on the edge of their seats.
guidance: Keep the pace moving—something should happen in every paragraph
Use strong, specific action verbs (sprinted, not ran quickly)
Include moments of tension followed by brief release
Short paragraphs during action sequences (1-2 sentences)
Vary sentence length: short for action, medium for transition
End chapters/sections on cliffhangers or questions
Make obstacles concrete and immediate
Show physical stakes—what could go wrong?

pacing_techniques.action_scenes: Short sentences. Staccato rhythm. One action per sentence.
pacing_techniques.transition_scenes: Medium sentences. Brief rest. Setup next challenge.
pacing_techniques.tension_building: Longer sentences that... suddenly cut short.

avoid: characters stopping to think during danger

lyrical.label: Lyrical
lyrical.description: Poetic, musical prose with rhythm and imagery. Language as art.
guidance: Pay attention to the sound of words together
Use sensory details that evoke emotion
Metaphors and similes should illuminate, not decorate
Let language create atmosphere and mood
Use rhythm: alternate long flowing sentences with short punchy ones
Choose words for their sound as well as meaning
Create patterns through repetition with variation
Let silence and white space speak
